title: Q&A: What is in the global ‘roadmap’ for transitioning away from fossil fuels? - Carbon Brief
gist: Brazil's voluntary fossil-fuel transition roadmap, released a week before COP31, proposes a self-assessed 'Belém readiness index', four country archetypes and three phases to 2033, while accepting 1.5C overshoot. Experts welcome it as a political signal, but its COP31 uptake is unclear as Turkey and Australia emphasise electrification.

insights.claim: Brazil's COP30 presidency produced a voluntary roadmap on transitioning away from fossil fuels after the topic was kept out of COP30's negotiated outcome; it is outside the UN process and countries are not obliged to respond.
insights.speaker: Daisy Dunne
insights.so_what: A non-binding product means no direct policy force; influence depends on uptake at COP31 and in national plans.
insights.quote: This roadmap is voluntary and countries are not obligated to respond to its findings.

insights.claim: At COP30, 85 countries wanted a fossil-fuel roadmap in the formal outcome while an opposing group, claimed to be 84, resisted; Carbon Brief found errors in the informal list, implying the opposing bloc was likely smaller.
insights.speaker: Daisy Dunne
insights.so_what: The opposition may have been overstated, hinting at more latent support for fossil-fuel language than headlines suggested.

insights.claim: The roadmap was informed by an April conference in Santa Marta, Colombia co-hosted by Colombia and the Netherlands on barriers to transitioning away from fossil fuels.
insights.speaker: Daisy Dunne
insights.so_what: Shows a coalition of willing producers and consumers building momentum outside UN consensus.
insights.locator: At COP30, the presidency also announced

insights.claim: The roadmap says that after decades of delay the world can no longer limit warming to 1.5C without first 'overshooting' the target.
insights.speaker: Daisy Dunne
insights.so_what: Official acceptance of overshoot shifts planning toward carbon removal and adaptation.

insights.claim: The roadmap says the clean-energy transition is already underway and the policies needed to move away from fossil fuels already exist and are readily deployable.
insights.speaker: Daisy Dunne
insights.so_what: Frames the constraint as political will and finance, not technology.

insights.claim: The roadmap calls the transition 'as much a development question as a climate one, especially for emerging markets and developing economies'.
insights.speaker: Daisy Dunne
insights.so_what: Implies financing and development support will be conditions for EM energy transitions.
insights.quote: as much a development question as a climate one, especially for emerging markets and developing economies

insights.claim: A 'Belém readiness index' is a voluntary self-assessment letting countries gauge fossil-fuel dependency and transition capacity, sorting them into four archetypes that point to tailored policy levers rather than a one-size-fits-all answer.
insights.speaker: Daisy Dunne
insights.so_what: Archetype segmentation could steer where transition finance and technology cooperation are targeted.

insights.claim: The roadmap sets three phases: to 2028 focus on institutions and long-term signals; 2028-2030 on physical transformation of energy systems around the next NDCs; 2031-2033 on scaling up, ending a decade after COP28's call.
insights.speaker: Daisy Dunne
insights.so_what: Sequencing implies near-term policy signals first, with capital deployment concentrated after 2028.
insights.locator: The roadmap calls for action in three distinct

insights.claim: Natalie Jones of IISD says the roadmap is an important political signal that the transition remains on the international agenda and gives governments practical guidance to plan in ways that strengthen energy security and protect livelihoods.
insights.speaker: Natalie Jones (IISD)
insights.so_what: Experts view it as agenda-preserving rather than a binding step.

insights.claim: Avantika Goswami says the roadmap is a 'unique and consultative method of multilateralism' led by a developing country, and countries should chart pathways in line with historical responsibility and current capacity.
insights.speaker: Avantika Goswami (CSE)
insights.so_what: Equity-based framing means developed-country finance obligations will feature in negotiations.
insights.quote: a “unique and consultative method of multilateralism”

insights.claim: Ploy Achakulwisut says exposure-capacity archetypes can support more targeted international cooperation by aligning finance, technology, capacity-building and technical assistance with country-specific needs.
insights.speaker: Ploy Achakulwisut
insights.so_what: Archetypes could become the organising logic for transition-finance allocation.

insights.claim: COP31 co-presidents Turkey and Australia target raising electricity's share of global final energy consumption from almost 24% in 2023 to 35% by 2035; Corrêa do Lago called this complementary to the fossil-fuel roadmap.
insights.speaker: Daisy Dunne
insights.so_what: An electrification target of 35% by 2035 is a concrete demand signal for power, grids and electrified end-uses.

insights.claim: Carbon Brief understands some parties see Turkey and Australia's electrification focus as a way to avoid rehashing the contentious fossil-fuel debates from COP30.
insights.speaker: Daisy Dunne
insights.so_what: Suggests fossil-fuel language may be sidelined at COP31 in favour of less divisive electrification goals.

insights.claim: Brazil's team was reluctant to predict how COP31 will take up the roadmap, with Ana Toni 'hoping for the best', and Corrêa do Lago pointing to existing COP28 consensus and instruments.
insights.speaker: Daisy Dunne
insights.so_what: No clear pathway into COP31 outcomes lowers the odds of fast formal adoption.
insights.locator: Both Corrêa do Lago and Toni

insights.claim: Jones argues COP31 should see more governments announce national fossil-fuel transition roadmaps, formally recognise the global roadmap, and route its findings into the second global stocktake, with vulnerable fossil-revenue-dependent countries needing international finance to diversify.
insights.speaker: Natalie Jones (IISD)
insights.so_what: Names the concrete asks that would turn the roadmap into policy, and the finance needs of fossil-dependent economies.
